replacements.FORMAL_RQ1_NARRATIVE: Across the 6 boundary-eligible locked projects, SEAC obtained boundary F1 0.5673 (95% CI [0.4708, 0.6488]); the strongest non-SEAC boundary baseline was Structure-only at 0.5032. The absolute SEAC-minus-baseline difference was +0.0640 (paired 95% CI [0.0313, 0.0956], Holm-adjusted p=0.4375), and SEAC had the higher project-level F1 on 6/6 projects.
replacements.FORMAL_RQ2_RQ3_NARRATIVE: SEAC achieved unit MRR 0.7937 and span MRR 0.8561. The strongest non-SEAC retrieval baseline was Structure-only with unit MRR 0.7290, an observed SEAC-minus-baseline difference of +0.0647. The prespecified confirmatory comparison against LlamaIndex sentence gave a paired mean difference of +0.1003 (95% CI [0.0042, 0.2008], exact two-sided p=0.0625); SEAC had higher project-level MRR on 5/6 retrieval-eligible locked projects. Its Hit@5 was 0.9520.
replacements.FORMAL_RQ4_NARRATIVE: The largest observed unit-MRR change relative to full SEAC occurred for No table-row children (−0.1084). Its paired SEAC-minus-ablation difference was +0.1084 (95% CI [0.0351, 0.2045], secondary-family Holm-adjusted p=1.0000). The complete table is reported because a component is not treated as causally necessary solely from the largest observed drop.
replacements.FORMAL_RQ5_NARRATIVE: Relative to the strongest non-SEAC retrieval baseline (Structure-only), SEAC used 5.50× as many retrieval vectors. Its pooled mean query latency differed by +5.7410 ms, while total locked-set chunking and indexing times were 112.11 s and 351.12 s, respectively.
